Hierarchical Bayes for Unit-Level Small Area Estimation

Source: R/hb_unit.R
hb_unit.Rd

Estimates small area parameters using unit-level Hierarchical Bayesian models (Battese-Harter-Fuller model and generalized linear mixed models) with Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations (INLA) or by full MCMC (jax_engine(), NumPyro NUTS). Supports Gaussian, Binomial (logistic regression for binary unit responses), and Poisson likelihoods, with optional spatial random effect structures (BYM2, Besag) and finite population adjustments.

Usage

hb_unit(
  formula,
  unit_data,
  Xpop,
  domain_var,
  popsize_var = NULL,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson"),
  spatial = c("none", "bym2", "besag"),
  W = NULL,
  popnmean_xpop = NULL,
  engine = "inla",
  print_result = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

An object of class formula specifying the unit-level fixed-effects model (e.g., y ~ x1 + x2).

unit_data

A data.frame containing the unit-level survey sample data.

Xpop

A data.frame containing auxiliary population information for all domains (either domain population means or unit-level population records). Must contain the domain identifier specified by domain_var.

domain_var

Character string specifying the column name for the domain identifier in both unit_data and Xpop.

popsize_var

Optional character string specifying the column name for domain population sizes (\(N_d\)) in Xpop. If provided, finite population adjustment \(\hat{\bar{Y}}_d = f_d \bar{y}_{d,s} + (1 - f_d) \hat{\mu}_{d,r}\) is computed, where \(f_d = n_d / N_d\). If NULL, the superpopulation expectation \(\hat{\bar{Y}}_d = \bar{X}_d^\top \hat{\beta} + \hat{u}_d\) is reported.

family

Character string specifying the response likelihood. Options:

  • "gaussian": Continuous response (Battese-Harter-Fuller model, default).

  • "binomial": Binary / Bernoulli response (0 or 1, e.g. poverty indicator).

  • "poisson": Count response (non-negative integer).

The domain means of "binomial" and "poisson" are approximate and biased; see Details.

spatial

Character string specifying the spatial random effect structure across domains:

  • "none": Non-spatial independent and identically distributed (IID) domain effects (default).

  • "bym2": Scaled Besag-York-Mollié 2 spatial model (Riebler et al., 2016).

  • "besag": Intrinsic Conditional Autoregressive (ICAR) spatial model.

W

Proximity or spatial adjacency matrix. Can be a square matrix, Matrix, or spdep nb or listw object. Dimensions must match the total number of unique domains in Xpop. Required when spatial != "none".

popnmean_xpop

Optional matrix or data frame of auxiliary population means per domain. If NULL (default), means are extracted directly from Xpop.

engine

Estimation engine: "inla" (default) or an inla_engine() object, or "jax" or a jax_engine() object for MCMC (see the section Engines). An inla_engine() holds the approximation strategy, the priors (prior_prec, default half-normal with the scale of the unit responses for family = "gaussian", see inla_engine(); prior_phi for BYM2), scale_model and further INLA::inla() arguments. The Gaussian model is fitted in INLA's "classic" mode, the binomial and Poisson models in INLA's default "compact" mode (for them classic was much slower: 72 s against 2.6 s for 4000 binary units); inla_engine(inla.mode = ) selects a mode.

print_result

Logical. If TRUE (default), prints a summary of results.

...

Deprecated. strategy, scale_model, prior_prec, prior_phi and arguments of INLA::inla() are now given to inla_engine(); passed here they are forwarded to it with a warning.

Value

An object of class c("fastsae_hb_unit", "fastsae_hb", "fastsae") containing:

  • df_hb: Data frame with domain estimates, including:

    • domain: Domain identifier.

    • hb: Estimated domain mean or proportion.

    • linear_pred: Posterior mean of domain linear predictor.

    • sd: Posterior standard deviation (standard error).

    • mse: Posterior Mean Squared Error (\(\text{sd}^2\)).

    • rse: Relative Standard Error (%).

    • ci_lower: 2.5% quantile of posterior credible interval.

    • ci_upper: 97.5% quantile of posterior credible interval.

    • samp_size: Sample size (\(n_d\)) in the domain (0 for unsampled).

    • pop_size: Population size (\(N_d\)), if popsize_var is provided.

    • estimated_total: Estimated domain population total (if popsize_var is provided).

    • sample_mean: Direct sample mean (\(\bar{y}_{d,s}\)).

    • random_effect: Posterior mean of domain random effect (\(\hat{u}_d\)).

  • estcoef: Data frame of estimated regression coefficients (posterior mean, sd, z-value, p-value, credible intervals).

  • hyperpar: Data frame of hyperparameter posterior estimates.

  • random_effect_var: Posterior mean of the domain random effect variance (\(\sigma_u^2\)). With few domains and the vague default prior its posterior is very skewed and INLA's summary of it is not accurate (on cornsoybean, 12 counties: about 70 against an exact posterior mean of 41 and median of 7, while the county means and SDs agree with the exact posterior). Do not read it as a REML estimate; the domain estimates in df_hb are the reliable output.

  • residual_var: Estimated residual variance (\(\sigma_e^2\), for Gaussian).

  • phi: Estimated spatial variance proportion (for BYM2).

  • goodness: Model fit metrics (DIC, WAIC, Marginal Log-Likelihood).

  • family: Response family used.

  • spatial: Spatial model type used.

  • unsampled_domains: Character vector of unsampled domain identifiers.

  • fit: Raw fitted INLA model object (the NumPyro output for jax_engine()).

  • engine, engine_spec: Engine name ("inla" or "jax") and its settings.

  • draws, rhat_max, device, elapsed_seconds: With jax_engine(), the domains x draws matrix of the domain means (if keep_draws = TRUE), the largest split R-hat (convergence is rhat_max < 1.05), the device used and the sampling time.

  • call: Matched function call.

Details

Non-Gaussian families. The non-sampled part of a domain mean is predicted at the mean covariates of the non-sampled units, \(g^{-1}(\bar x_{d,r}^\top\beta + u_d)\). For the identity link of "gaussian" this is the mean of \(x_j^\top\beta + u_d\) over the units. For the logit and log links of "binomial" and "poisson" it is not: the mean of \(g^{-1}(x_j^\top\beta + u_d)\) over the units differs from it whenever the covariates vary within the domain (for the log link it is larger by the factor \(E[\exp((x_j - \bar x)^\top\beta)] > 1\)). In a simulation with one normal covariate of within-domain variance 1, the domain means of the sampled domains were biased by -8% (binomial, slope 1.2) and -16% (Poisson, slope 0.6), and the 95% credible intervals covered the true means in 90% and 78% of the cases. Unbiased estimation needs the covariates of every population unit, as in the empirical best predictor of Molina and Rao (2010); a unit-level Xpop is currently averaged per domain. A warning is given for these families.

Engines

Both engines fit the same model from the sampled units and return the same structure. With jax_engine() the coefficients have normal priors (standard deviation 10, or 2.5 for "binomial") and the standard deviations of the domain effect and, for "gaussian", of the unit errors half-normal(1) priors, on the standardised response scale for "gaussian"; inla_engine() puts the vague log-gamma prior on the precisions. The domain means, SDs and 2.5%/97.5% quantiles are computed from the MCMC draws; with popsize_var each draw of the Gaussian domain mean includes the mean error of the non-sampled units, \(N(0, \sigma_e^2 / (N_d - n_d))\) for that draw of \(\sigma_e^2\) (the INLA engine adds its posterior mean to the variance and gives a normal interval).

On simulated data (30 domains, three unsampled) a Stan fit of the same model and priors gave domain means within 0.04 posterior SD and SDs within 5% for the Gaussian (also with BYM2), Bernoulli and Poisson models. With their own priors, hbsae::fSAE(method = "HB") (Gaussian, numerical integration over the variance ratio, flat priors) and the INLA engine gave domain means within 0.1 and 0.06 posterior SD. With few domains the prior of the domain variance matters: on cornsoybean (12 counties) the county SDs were 1.1-1.4 times those of INLA, whose log-gamma prior favours small variances, and 0.8-1.0 times those of hbsae.

References

  1. Molina, I., & Rao, J. N. K. (2010). Small area estimation of poverty indicators. Canadian Journal of Statistics, 38(3), 369-385.

  2. Battese, G. E., Harter, R. M., & Fuller, W. A. (1988). An error-components model for prediction of county crop areas using survey and satellite data. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 83(401), 28-36.

  3. Rao, J. N. K., & Molina, I. (2015). Small Area Estimation (2nd ed.). John Wiley & Sons.

  4. Riebler, A., Sørbye, S. H., Simpson, D., & Rue, H. (2016). An intuitive Bayesian spatial model for disease mapping that accounts for scaling. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 25(4), 1145-1165.

  5. Rue, H., Martino, S., & Chopin, N. (2009). Approximate Bayesian inference for latent Gaussian models by using integrated nested Laplace approximations. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 71(2), 319-392.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(fastsae)
  data(cornsoybean)
  data(cornsoybeanmeans)

  # Prepare auxiliary population means
  df_pop <- cornsoybeanmeans
  names(df_pop)[names(df_pop) == "MeanCornPixPerSeg"] <- "CornPix"
  names(df_pop)[names(df_pop) == "MeanSoyBeansPixPerSeg"] <- "SoyBeansPix"

  # Unit survey data
  df_sample <- cornsoybean
  names(df_sample)[names(df_sample) == "County"] <- "CountyIndex"

  # Fit unit-level Hierarchical Bayes model
  fit_hb_u <- hb_unit(
    formula = CornHec ~ CornPix + SoyBeansPix,
    unit_data = df_sample,
    Xpop = df_pop,
    domain_var = "CountyIndex",
    popsize_var = "PopnSegments"
  )
  print(fit_hb_u)
}
